_README: Work that is stopped, and the person who can start it again.
This is the hand-written half of the resume report, and it is deliberately small.
Everything an agent can derive — the branch, the dirty tree, the last commits, the
Supabase queue, the open notes — is derived by mobile/scripts/resume-status.mjs.
What cannot be derived is who is allowed to unblock a thing, so that is what lives
'blocked' without an owner is the failure this file exists to stop. An agent cannot
flip a connector toggle, paste a GitHub Actions secret, buy Lovable credits, put a
card through Razorpay or enable a branch ruleset. A report that says 'blocked on
Supabase' reads as 'try again later'; 'blocked on the owner enabling the connector
in this chat's settings' is an instruction someone can act on in ten seconds.
clearsWhen is a cheap OFFLINE probe of something that would be observably different
once the blocker is gone. The report prints MAY BE CLEAR when it fires; it never
edits this file, because a probe can be right about the filesystem and wrong about
the world. Kinds: manual | pathExists | pathMissing | grepPresent | grepAbsent |
Add an entry the moment you are stopped by something, not at the end of the session.
Set status to 'cleared' rather than deleting: a blocker that vanishes gets rediscovered.

blockers.what: generate-handwritten-notes cannot be deployed (job sb-physio-flowchart): 3 of 11 cached Physiology notes have no flowchart, which is the section a student actually writes down.
blockers.blockedOn: a route to Supabase. No agent sandbox has one — the egress gateway answers 403 to the CONNECT itself, before any credential is offered, so a personal access token is not an unblock.
blockers.owner: the app owner, in two ways: enable the Supabase connector for the chat (Claude Code or Antigravity), or push so that .github/workflows/supabase-tasks.yml runs on a GitHub runner, which does have a route.
blockers.remedy: cd mobile && npm run supabase:status, then follow .claude/skills/supabase-resume/SKILL.md. If the connector is missing, report WHICH: connected:false is a reconnect, connected:true + enabledInChat:false is a toggle in the chat's connector settings. No tool can flip it.
blockers.clearedBy: A route exists after all, and the standing claim that no sandbox has one is now too strong. A session holding the Supabase MCP connector can reach an edge function WITHOUT any direct egress: the `http` extension (v1.6) is installed on this project, so Postgres itself makes the request. select http_post('https://pmtgeydtqypwrypshhsx.supabase.co/functions/v1/<slug>', <json body>::text, 'application/json') — raise the timeout first with http_set_curlopt('CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS','170000') or a model call will be cut off at the default. generate-handwritten-notes has verify_jwt:false so it needs no Authorization header. Build the body from the row itself with jsonb_build_object so a large note never has to travel through an agent's context. This is what made the sb-physio-flowchart backfill possible from a sandbox, and it is also how the repair was diagnosed: query_logs on source='function_logs' reads the function's own console output back.
blockers.stillTrue: The egress gateway still refuses a direct CONNECT to *.supabase.co and api.supabase.com from the sandbox, so supabase-js, the CLI and physio-flowchart-backfill.mjs --run still cannot work here. What changed is that the CONNECTOR is a usable route to both SQL and the functions, not only to SQL. Deploying a function still needs the connector's deploy_edge_function; the http extension cannot do that (the Management API needs a personal access token).

blockers.what: Google Sign-In needs an Android OAuth client whose SHA-1 matches the certificate that signed the running build. Play App Signing means real users run a build signed by GOOGLE's key, not the upload key — so registering only the upload key gives sign-in that works in every test build and fails for every real user.
blockers.blockedOn: three Android OAuth clients existing in Google Cloud: deployment (54:F7:27:...), internal/upload (CE:EA:8A:...), and .debug.
blockers.owner: the app owner, in the Google Cloud console. An agent cannot create OAuth clients.
blockers.remedy: mobile/OAUTH-SETUP.md has all three with their exact values.
blockers.evidence2026_09_04: Narrowed with live data: auth.identities holds 322 google identities, most recent sign-in 2026-09-01. The Supabase Google provider, Web client ID and secret are therefore correct and working (those are the web app's browser flow). The app's DEVELOPER_ERROR is thrown by Google Play Services ON THE DEVICE before Supabase is contacted, and means no Android OAuth client matches the APK's (package name, SHA-1). Nothing in this repo or in Supabase can fix it. Do not re-investigate the Supabase side.
blockers.confirmedFromArtifact2026_09_04: The internal APK's own certificate, read out of the build with apksigner rather than taken from a doc (run 33890078552, release internal-144): package com.aistudio.mbbsqbank.aycxvd, SHA-1 ceea8a41bb0778c47826d88fcce02cc9eb294068 = CE:EA:8A:41:BB:07:78:C4:78:26:D8:8F:CC:E0:2C:C9:EB:29:40:68. That matches OAUTH-SETUP.md's client #2 exactly, so the upload-key value there is verified. Client #1 (Play App Signing) still cannot be read from here — it only exists in the Play Console.

blockers.what: Nothing on GitHub currently stops this repository, or the main branch, being deleted. check:repo-intact guards the contents of a checkout; it cannot guard the repository.
blockers.blockedOn: repository settings. The GitHub admin and Actions APIs are denied by the agent proxy, and repository deletion protection is an owner-only setting in any case.
blockers.owner: the app owner (or an org admin). The exact click paths are in .agents/REPO-PROTECTION.md.
blockers.remedy: Settings > Rules > Rulesets > New branch ruleset, target main, tick Restrict deletions and Restrict force pushes. Then Settings > General > Danger Zone and confirm who can delete. An off-GitHub mirror is the only real backstop.
